<SPAN 2>This Vendor/Supplier Non-disclosure Agreement (“Agreement”) is made and entered into as of , 20 , by and between , a , the principal address of which is , (“Recipient”) and Oceaneering International, Inc., a Delaware corporation, the principal address of which is 11911 FM 529, Houston, Texas 77041, USA (“Oceaneering”).</SPAN 2>
<SPAN 3>It is the intention of the parties to this Agreement to facilitate discussions regarding possible transactions between the parties by the protection from unauthorized disclosure or use of the Confidential Information (defined below). </SPAN 3><SPAN 4>Therefore, the parties agree as follows:</SPAN 4>
<SPAN 5>1. For the purposes of this Agreement, “Confidential Information” shall mean any information disclosed by Oceaneering, whether in writing, orally, visually or otherwise, including but not limited to business plans, contractual, engineering, financial, sales, marketing and operational information, product specifications, technical data, trade secrets, know-how, ideas and concepts of Oceaneering or third parties. </SPAN 5><SPAN 6>Confidential Information excludes, however, information which: </SPAN 6><SPAN 7>(i) is or becomes known or available to Recipient without restriction from a source other than Oceaneering with a legal right to disclose the same to Recipient; </SPAN 7><SPAN 8>(ii) is, or without violating the terms of this Agreement becomes, generally available to the public; or </SPAN 8><SPAN 9>(iii) is developed by Recipient independently of the information disclosed hereunder.</SPAN 9>
<SPAN 10>2. With respect to all Confidential Information disclosed hereunder, Recipient agrees that from and after the date of this Agreement, Recipient shall not:</SPAN 10>
<SPAN 11>a. use the Confidential Information except for purposes of its business relationship with Oceaneering (the “Authorized Purpose”); or</SPAN 11>
<SPAN 12>b. disclose the Confidential Information to any third party except: </SPAN 12><SPAN 13>(i) for directors, officers, managers, employees, consultants, contractors and professional advisors of Recipient (collectively its “Representatives”) who need to know the Confidential Information for the Authorized Purpose and who are subject to an existing obligation to, or enter into an agreement with, Recipient not to disclose Confidential Information; and </SPAN 13><SPAN 14>(ii) as may be authorized in writing in advance by an officer of Oceaneering.</SPAN 14>
<SPAN 15>3. Recipient shall require its Representatives who receive any Confidential Information to comply with the terms and conditions of this Agreement and Recipient shall be responsible for their compliance herewith. </SPAN 15><SPAN 16>Recipient shall use at least the same degree of care to protect the confidentiality and ensure the proper use of the Confidential Information as Recipient uses with respect to its information of a similar kind or nature, but in no event less than reasonable care.</SPAN 16>
<SPAN 17>4. Oceaneering grants no rights in or to the Confidential Information. </SPAN 17><SPAN 18>All Confidential Information shall remain the sole property of Oceaneering.</SPAN 18>
<SPAN 19>5. No contract or agreement providing for any transaction or any commitment to enter into a transaction shall be deemed to exist by reason of this Agreement.</SPAN 19>
<SPAN 20>6. Any provision to the contrary notwithstanding, Recipient’s obligations under this Agreement are subject to any disclosure requirement of law, regulation or legal process, but only to the extent of such requirement. </SPAN 20><SPAN 21>Recipient shall promptly notify </SPAN 21><SPAN 22>Oceaneering of any such requirement, cooperate fully with Oceaneering’s requests to prevent or minimize the effect of such disclosure, and make all reasonable efforts to have such disclosures placed under a protective order or otherwise obtain confidential treatment of the Confidential Information.</SPAN 22>
<SPAN 23>7. THE CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION IS DISCLOSED “AS IS” WITHOUT ANY REPRESENTATION, WARRANTY, ASSURANCE, GUARANTEE, OR INDUCEMENT OF ANY KIND, INCLUDING WITHOUT LIMITATION ANY EXPRESS OR IMPLIED WARRANTY OF COMPLETENESS, ACCURACY, MERCHANTABILITY, SUITABILITY, NON-INFRINGEMENT OR FITNESS FOR PURPOSE.</SPAN 23>
<SPAN 24>8. Upon Oceaneering’s written request, Recipient shall promptly: </SPAN 24><SPAN 25>(i) deliver to Oceaneering and cease to use all Confidential Information in Recipient’s (including its Representatives’) possession, custody or control; or </SPAN 25><SPAN 26>(ii) destroy the same and delete all electronic records containing the Confidential Information, provided that Oceaneering may require Recipient to certify in writing such destruction and deletion.</SPAN 26>
<SPAN 27>9. Recipient agrees that money damages would not be a sufficient remedy for breach of this Agreement and that, in addition to all other remedies, Oceaneering shall be entitled to specific performance and injunctive or other equitable relief as a remedy for such breach.</SPAN 27>
<SPAN 28>10. This Agreement sets forth the complete and exclusive statement of the parties’ agreement with respect to the subject matter hereof. </SPAN 28><SPAN 29>This Agreement may not be waived or modified except pursuant to a written agreement signed by the parties. </SPAN 29><SPAN 30>Any waiver or forbearance on one occasion shall have no effect on any other occasion.</SPAN 30>
<SPAN 31>11. Any provision hereof which is found to be unenforceable or contrary to applicable law shall be deemed stricken from this Agreement and the other terms and conditions hereof shall remain in full force and effect.</SPAN 31>
<SPAN 32>12. This Agreement shall bind and benefit the parties and their respective successors and assigns. </SPAN 32><SPAN 33>Recipient’s obligations under this Agreement shall survive any termination hereof.</SPAN 33>
<SPAN 34>13. This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of Texas (excluding its conflicts-of-laws principles). </SPAN 34><SPAN 35>The parties consent to the jurisdiction of the state and federal courts situated in Houston, Harris County, Texas.</SPAN 35>
<SPAN 36>Executed on the dates set forth below but effective as of the date first written above.</SPAN 36>
<SPAN 37>Recipient: Oceaneering International, Inc.</SPAN 37>
<SPAN 38>By: By:</SPAN 38>

The candidate evidence is span 5, which defines Confidential Information as including technical data, trade secrets, etc. However, the NDA doesn't explicitly mention reverse engineering. So, there's no direct mention of reverse engineering, so the answer would be NotMentioned.

Next, nda-16: "Receiving Party shall destroy or return some Confidential Information upon the termination of Agreement." The evidence here is span 26, which talks about destroying or deleting Confidential Information upon Oceaneering's request. But the hypothesis mentions termination of the agreement, while the NDA refers to a written request. So, it's not exactly the same, so NotMentioned.

For nda-15: "Agreement shall not grant Receiving Party any right to Confidential Information." Span 17 states that Oceaneering grants no rights, so this is directly supported. Therefore, Entailment.

nda-10: "Receiving Party shall not disclose the fact that Agreement was agreed or negotiated." The NDA doesn't mention anything about disclosing the existence of the agreement, so NotMentioned.

nda-2: "Confidential Information shall only include technical information." Span 5 lists various types including technical data, but also business plans, financial info, etc. So the hypothesis is too narrow, hence Contradiction.

nda-1: "All Confidential Information shall be expressly identified by the Disclosing Party." The NDA defines Confidential Information as any disclosed information, not necessarily requiring express identification. So NotMentioned.

nda-19: "Some obligations of Agreement may survive termination of Agreement." Span 33 says obligations survive termination, so Entailment.

nda-3: "Confidential Information may include verbally conveyed information." Span 5 includes "orally" as a method, so Entailment.

nda-18: "Receiving Party shall not solicit some of Disclosing Party's representatives." No mention of solicitation, so NotMentioned.

nda-17: "Receiving Party may create a copy of some Confidential Information in some circumstances." The NDA doesn't mention copying, so NotMentioned.

nda-8: "Receiving Party shall notify Disclosing Party in case Receiving Party is required by law, regulation or judicial process to disclose any Confidential Information." Span 20 mentions notifying Oceaneering of legal requirements, so Entailment.

nda-13: "Receiving Party may acquire information similar to Confidential Information from a third party." The NDA allows information from other sources if they have a right, so NotMentioned.

nda-5: "Receiving Party may share some Confidential Information with some of Receiving Party's employees." Span 13 includes employees as Representatives, so Entailment.

nda-4: "Receiving Party shall not use any Confidential Information for any purpose other than the purposes stated in Agreement." Span 11 restricts use to Authorized Purpose, so Entailment.

I need to make sure each decision is based solely on the provided text and not external knowledge. Also, check if any spans are missing or if the reasoning is correct. For example, nda-12's span 9 says independent development is excluded, so the hypothesis is allowed, hence Entailment. Similarly, nda-2 is contradicted because the definition includes non-technical info. Each hypothesis must be checked against the exact text and the spans provided.
